subject: EU edge maintenance — temporary SLA response-window & rotation fallback
messages:
From: Lena Hoffmann <lena@acme-telemetry.de>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-11 09:12 +0100
Subject: Planned EU edge maintenance — potential temporary P2 window impact

Hi Grace,

Quick heads-up from our side: Acme Telemetry (Helios Cloud network) has scheduled a multi-region edge maintenance next week (Apr 14–15 UTC) across two EU PoPs. We expect rolling restarts on the edge proxies which may increase tail latency for cross-PoP traffic for short windows (up to ~12–18 mins per PoP).

We ran the initial risk assessment with Helios and they asked whether Redwood can support a short-term SLA modification for P2 response windows during the maintenance windows (specifically an allowance for 30–45 additional minutes for non-P1 triage). They also want a documented fallback plan for on-call routing to avoid P1 spillover.

Can your team confirm feasibility and share a proposed temporary routing / on-call rotation that keeps P1 coverage intact while accepting a narrower P2 guarantee? Helios wants something they can attach to a one-off amendment (DocuSign).

Thanks —
Lena
Head of Integrations, Acme Telemetry

--
Attachment: helios-maintenance-schedule.xlsx (stub)

From: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffmann <lena@acme-telemetry.de>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-11 10:03 +01:00
Subject: Re: Planned EU edge maintenance — potential temporary P2 window impact

Lena / team,

Thanks for the heads-up. Short answer: yes — we can accept a temporary P2 window adjustment for the maintenance windows with a formal amendment. High-level proposal below:

- Maintenance windows: Apr 14 22:00–Apr 15 06:00 UTC (rolling across PoPs)
- P1: unchanged (immediate on-call page + 15-minute SLA for acknowledgement)
- P2: temporary allowance +45 minutes for initial triage during the maintenance window only
- On-call changes: implement staggered rota for the maintenance nights so we have overlap between EU and US responders (see attached CSV for proposed shifts)
- Fallback routing: redirect traffic to the nearest compatible model variant in a different region if tail latency crosses 1.5s 95th percentile; this limits user impact and prevents P1 escalation cascade

I attached a short runbook and the proposed staggered-shift CSV. If this looks acceptable, we can prepare the DocuSign amendment and schedule a 30-minute sync with Helios ops + our on-call leads.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Karthik to confirm the technical fallback (model-routing + KV cache considerations) and any latency caveats.
2) Marcus to confirm on-call availability and approve the staggered shifts.
3) Prepare amendment + schedule sync (I can host).

Grace Oconnor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: eu-maintenance-runbook-v1.pdf (stub), oncall-staggered-shifts.csv (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Lena Hoffmann <lena@acme-telemetry.de>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12 08:27 +05:30
Subject: Re: Planned EU edge maintenance — potential temporary P2 window impact

Grace / Lena,

Quick technical notes — I validated the fallback routing approach:
- We can route to a compatible model variant in a neighboring region (quantized variant) without losing session continuity if we snapshot and warm a KV prefix cache. Warm-up cost estimated at ~1–2 minutes per model per node.
- Risk: if traffic spikes coincide with the warm-up, we may see token-latency blips; mitigation is to pre-warm most-used tokens and keep a small buffer pool of standby replicas (we'll reserve burst capacity for Apr 14–15).
- No changes required to tenant config, but we'll add a temporary policy tag so routing happens only during the maintenance window.

I attached the edge-fallback-policy doc with the exact kernel selection and cache-warm sequence. Marcus — if the shifts in the CSV are workable, I'll schedule a dry-run on Apr 13 22:00 UTC to validate warm-up times.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: edge-fallback-policy.md (stub)

From: Helios Cloud Ops <ops@helioscloud.com>

Cc: Paul Greene <paul.greene@finpulse.com>
Date: 2026-04-13 14:05 +02:00
Subject: Re: Planned EU edge maintenance — potential temporary P2 window impact

Thanks — that plan looks reasonable to Helios. A few asks before we proceed:

1) We require a one-off amendment to the SLO appendix for Apr 14–15 that documents the temporary P2 window and the fallback routing protections. Can you send a DocuSign-ready draft?
2) Helios procurement requests a contingency credit clause in case a sustained degradation >1 hour occurs during the windows (simple pro-rata credit).
3) Please include the dry-run results as an addendum after Apr 13; we'll want evidence to attach.

I've opened a support ticket on our side (HELIOS-7891) and added Paul from FinPulse (they consume the same Redwood routes) — they wanted to be looped in on the amendment.

If you can share the DocuSign link by EOD Apr 13 UTC we can route internally and sign.

—Helios Ops

- Run the dry-run tonight (Apr 13 22:00 UTC) and share results in SUP-5217. If the dry-run shows warm-up >2 minutes, we'll expand the buffer pool as a mitigation.
- Implement the staggered on-call shifts for Apr 14–15 per the CSV; Marcus has confirmed coverage and Evelyn will be the escalation lead during the EU window.

Action items now:

We will treat this as a focused, one-off exception with rollback to standard SLOs immediately after Apr 15 06:00 UTC.
